strings.name: He Xiaopeng
strings.role: UC co-founder and XPeng chairman and CEO
strings.summary: He Xiaopeng moved from mobile internet entrepreneurship to smart electric vehicles, working at UC, Alibaba and XPeng. He leads strategy and business; browsers, vehicles, driver assistance and robots are developed by teams and partners.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Company founding and personal appointments, investment agreements and closing, listing structures, driver assistance, demonstration permits and future production plans are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded UC and contributed to XPeng, connecting mobile internet entrepreneurship with smart vehicles and automated-driving applications.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor’s degree in computer science from South China University of Technology, July 1999.
strings.facts.f2.label: Cross-industry career
strings.facts.f2.value: Co-founded UC, worked at Alibaba and entered automotive management; roles from different periods are not presented as concurrent.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Mobile internet entrepreneurship
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped establish UC and run its products, carrying browser and mobile-service experience into later work.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Smart vehicles and technology partnerships
strings.highlights.h2.text: Leads XPeng and industry partnerships; corporate technology is not his sole invention, and driver assistance is not unrestricted driverless operation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses quarterly results and technology plans
strings.timeline.t1.text: Comments on growth and robot plans in unaudited results. The quarter still records a net loss; demonstration approval and a year-end production target do not mean full commercialization is complete.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Volkswagen minority investment closes
strings.timeline.t2.text: XPeng announces completed subscription by a Volkswagen entity, holding about 4.99% immediately afterward; distinct from the July 26 agreement announcement and not an acquisition of control.
strings.timeline.t3.title: XPeng completes Hong Kong dual-primary listing
strings.timeline.t3.text: Class A ordinary shares list on Hong Kong’s Main Board, distinct from American depositary shares traded in New York.
strings.timeline.t4.title: XPeng ADSs begin US trading
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company’s American depositary shares list on the NYSE as XPEV; company financing is separate from personal income.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes XPeng chairman and CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Takes automotive leadership after Alibaba; this appointment date is not the company’s founding date.
strings.timeline.t6.title: UC fully integrated into Alibaba
strings.timeline.t6.text: Alibaba announces acquisition of the remaining UC interests. He subsequently works within the group; the new business group leader named that day is Yu Yongfu.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-founds UC
strings.timeline.t7.text: Helps establish the mobile internet company; his official biography dates his product presidency from January 2005 to June 2014.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns computer science degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduates from South China University of Technology, then enters software and internet work.
